title: TD Memory Quality and Reliability PhD Intern
location: US, California, Folsom; US, California, Santa Clara; US, Oregon, Hillsboro
description: Job Details: Job Description: About the Team The Technology Development (TD) Quality and Reliability organization plays a critical role in enabling the successful deployment of next-generation semiconductor technologies through silicon-based quality, reliability, and technology readiness assessments. The Memory Quality and Reliability team works closely with Design, Device Engineering, Product Development Engineering (PDE), and Yield organizations to develop, characterize, and certify SRAM, Register File (RF), and Fuse technologies for advanced process nodes. The team supports key technology certification and PDK release milestones through memory characterization, silicon data analysis, predictive modeling, and risk assessment. Role Overview As a TD Memory Quality and Reliability Intern, you will collaborate with experienced engineers to evaluate advanced memory technologies and help drive technology readiness for future Intel Foundry process nodes. This role offers hands-on experience in memory characterization, silicon data analytics, statistical modeling, and semiconductor technology development. You will contribute to projects that support technology certification decisions by analyzing silicon data, developing predictive models, and assessing memory performance across various operating conditions. Responsibilities Responsibilities may include, but are not limited to: Analyze silicon characterization data from SRAM, Register File (RF), and Fuse memory test structures to identify performance trends, variability, and potential risks. Support memory characterization activities across voltage, temperature, and process conditions. Perform data analysis, visualization, and reporting using Python, JMP, or similar analytical tools. Develop and enhance statistical models for Vmin/Vmax prediction and technology readiness assessments. Support Silicon-to-Simulation (Sil2Sim) correlation studies and memory characterization methodologies. Generate technical reports and contribute to technology certification reviews. Collaborate with cross-functional teams including Design, Device Engineering, Process Integration, Product Development Engineering, and Yield Engineering. Assist with risk assessment activities and technology certification milestones. Present data-driven findings and recommendations to engineering teams and project stakeholders. Qualifications: Minimum Qualifications Currently pursuing a Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering or a related field. Basic knowledge of semiconductor devices, microelectronics, or integrated circuit design. Programming or scripting experience using Python or similar languages. Experience analyzing technical, scientific, or research data through academic projects, research activities, or previous internships. Strong academic performance with a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher required. Preferred Qualifications Coursework, research, or experience in one or more of the following areas: SRAM or memory technologies Semiconductor device physics VLSI design Statistics, machine learning, or data science Semiconductor process technology Experience with: Python, Pandas, and NumPy JMP or other statistical analysis tools Data visualization and statistical modeling techniques Large-scale data analysis and predictive modeling Additional experience in memory architectures, silicon characterization, reliability assessment, or semiconductor test methodologies is highly desirable. What You Will Learn During this internship, you will gain exposure to: Advanced SRAM, RF, and Fuse memory technologies Memory characterization and certification methodologies Silicon data analytics and statistical modeling techniques Vmin/Vmax evaluation and predictive model development Technology qualification and certification processes Cross-functional semiconductor technology development workflows Silicon-based decision making for technology readiness and risk assessment Job Type: Student / Intern Shift: Shift 1 (United States of America) Primary Location: US, California, Folsom Additional Locations: US, California, Santa Clara, US, Oregon, Hillsboro Posting Statement: All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, religious creed, sex, national origin, ancestry, age, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, military and veteran status, marital status, pregnancy, gender, gender expression, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by local law, regulation, or ordinance. title: Research Scientist Intern - Video Recsys
description: Meta is seeking AI Research interns to join our Video Recommendations team within Facebook. Videos (Reels, long videos, and Live streams) are increasingly the formats of choice across the social media industry, and making all these formats successful is a top priority for Facebook, and the core mission owned by this org. Time spent on Facebook watching videos accounts for 1.2+ Billion hours/day, which is over 56% of time spent globally on the App, and this number is expected to continue growing. This team is directly in charge of recommending all sorts of videos to users, powered by our large-scale unified video recommendation models. In this role, you will work on Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI): building AI agents that autonomously propose, run, evaluate, and learn from improvements to these models, closing the loop between ML experimentation and model quality. Our interns will have the opportunity to frame practical, high-impact challenges in recommendation into rigorous machine learning problems, and bring their own expertise to build innovative solutions under the guidance of our Research Scientists and Software Engineers. More concretely, you will develop an agent-driven RSI prototype that continuously proposes, evaluates, and refines improvements for a selected video recommendation task. The scope spans training data improvement, environment and experiment setup, automated offline model evaluation, and feedback collection from model quality signals such as normalized entropy (NE) and recall. You will use experiment outcomes to improve both the agent's intervention strategy and its evaluation criteria, and deliver a working end-to-end prototype with evidence against a fixed baseline. Work will be mentored by the team, with production changes and online experiments subject to owner review and approval. Our internships are twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year.
